chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Breaking the bootleggers and the record business
summary: Musician-owned labels cannot beat big distributors; Mingus plans to bootleg the bootleggers' records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: (Inaudible.)
That's all right, I'm fine. We used to talk every once in a while about politics and stuff. Do you still follow that?
(Inaudible.)
Yeah, on the phone or whatever.
Yeah. Only not recently. Saw you following Lindsay around.
Huh?
Saw you following Mayor -- on television one time, saw you with your band, following Mayor Lindsay.

Oh, yeah, yeah. Boy, he was nuts about us. What about change of control? We went into this very briefly the last time. You had your own record label, Straight is owned by musicians. A few of them, not many. Is there really any chance of breaking a big company, big distributor tie-up?
I just feel tired when you say that, because it's almost impossible. The main thing to break is the bootleg guys.
Yeah.
That's the ones to break. The ones who'd
steal from the companies and put it out on another label. Like (inaudible).
I'm not surprised.
Somebody walk in with some guns, they'd shoot him, that's all.
Yeah.
You have to become as bad as they do. It's like this kid who (inaudible) I saw. Three men walked in and killed his father and mother. She was an Indian and he was half Indian.
Yeah.

So he went out to try to catch them. He didn't know anything about a gun or anything. He ran into this guy who made guns. Taught him everything. He said, you've got to become like they do, like they are, to catch those guys. You've got to be like a snake. You've got to be able to go without food, you've got to be able to live in the gutter.
Yeah.

Hide in mud. And these people that are robbing, to catch them, you've got to be as dirty as they are. For instance, I could take one of their records and record it, and let them sue me, which they could never do.
Yeah.
That's what I'm planning on doing, if I live.
Yeah. You really think you'd do it?
Yeah, just go and buy one of their records, (inaudible) put another name on it and advertise on television. I got somebody to back me already.
That makes sense. Do you plan to --
(Inaudible.)
